problem:
In a particular business bank account, the rate at which money is being deposited into the account is given by the function

$$
r(t)=600(2t+1)^{3},
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in dollars per month, and $t>0$ is the number of months since the account was opened. When the account was first opened, the business owners placed an initial deposit of $$1\,000$ into the account.

How much money will be in the account after $3$ months?
worked_solution:
We're given a **rate of change** in the amount of money $r(t).$ 

To find the **total amount** of money in the account after $t$ months (call it $T(t)$), we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =T(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}r(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\,000+{\int }_{0}^{t}600(2x+1)^{3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To be sure that $T$ is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. 

We now let $t=3,$ and evaluate.

$$
\begin{aligned}T(3) & =1\,000+{\int }_{0}^{3}600(2x+1)^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\,000+600{\int }_{0}^{3}(2x+1)^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\,000+\frac{600}{2\cdot 4}{(2t+1)^{4}|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =1\,000+75{(2t+1)^{4}|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =1\,000+75[(2(3)+1)^{4}-(2(0)+1)^{4}] \\  & =1\,000+75[{7}^{4}-{1}^{4}] \\  & =1\,000+75[2\,401-1] \\  & =1\,000+75[2\,400] \\  & =181\,000\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there will be $$181\,000$ in the account after $3$ months.
